For each connective semantics and reading, (-3 : Int).toNat = 0 (fToNatNeg) is true in Lean, false for oneJ and human-undefined.
nonvacuity_witness: No propositional hypotheses (vacuous). trap_cast_placement quantifies over c : Conn and trap_toNat_neg over c : Conn and r : SubReading, all inhabited; the quantifier over environments rho inside trap_cast_placement is part of its conclusion. natCast_sub_eq_iff_le (a b : Nat) is a biconditional without premises, and both of its sides take both truth values: at a = 1, b = 0 the cast equation holds (0 <= 1), and at a = 0, b = 1 it fails (NOT (1 <= 0)).
non_claims: The toy does not model where Lean's elaborator inserts coercions; which of the two cast placements a given Lean source statement elaborates to must be checked in Lean.

The first Lean value rests on truncated subtraction inside the cast ((0 : Nat) - 1 is 0 before it is cast), and (-3 : Int).toNat = 0 on the truncation of negative integers to 0. Readers bring a convention, not the absence of one: integer subtraction (the cast equation holds, as in the intValued reading), subtraction that panics below zero (no value; the closest toy outcome is the partialNat value, undefined), or wrapping unsigned subtraction followed by a widening cast (the cast of the largest machine value); for Int.toNat, an error, a saturating conversion (which also gives 0 here) or a bit-reinterpreting conversion. tier_rationale: The left-to-right well-definedness operator L is known to be stricter than the symmetric operator D (Darvas, Mehta and Rudich 2008); these are concrete instances for the checker guarded.
plain_claim: The set of formulas accepted by the syntactic checker guarded is not closed under rewrites that are equivalences in Lean's reading: with a b : Nat, b <= a AND a - b + b = a (fGuardFirst) is accepted while a - b + b = a AND b <= a (fGuardSecond) is rejected, and b <= a -> a - b + b = a (fSubAddCancelGuarded) is accepted while its contrapositive NOT (a - b + b = a) -> NOT (b <= a) (fContrapositive) is rejected, although each pair has the same total value under every junk record at every environment.
nonvacuity_witness: Concrete formulas; no hypotheses (vacuous).
non_claims: Concerns the checker's verdict, not semantic definedness. Whether a sound checker can restore closure depends on the connective semantics: under sequential connectives even the semantic class of everywhere-defined formulas fails closure under both rewrites (Toy.Junk.ce_seq_not_closed), so no checker sound for sequential connectives can accept both members of either pair; under strong Kleene connectives the class of everywhere-defined formulas is closed under both rewrites (Toy.Junk.definedEverywhere_kleene_closed), and a symmetric checker that lets later conjuncts or negated consequents supply facts is not defined or examined here.
Says nothing about closure under other Lean equivalences (associativity, distributivity, de Morgan) beyond the two shown.
